target_venue: Journal of Engineering and Applied Science
scientific_question: Do performance and model-superiority claims for severe felt-intensity classifiers remain supportable when data versioning, dependent-event splitting, temporal evaluation, paired uncertainty, and exact reconstruction are controlled?
intended_users: applied machine-learning engineers developing event-level classifiers
reviewers and auditors evaluating model-comparison claims
task_enabled: Perform a transparent retrospective audit of a declared classifier against fixed data, roles, baselines, metrics, uncertainty, and reproducibility gates without reconstructing a bespoke split.
decision_enabled: Decide whether a candidate is within the declared comparison contract and whether its Brier-score improvement over a reference is supported rather than a point-score fluctuation.
error_prevented: Prevents retrospective comparisons based on evolving catalogue versions, forbidden outcome-derived features, sequence-role overlap, temporal-cutoff violations, unquantified point rankings, or unreproducible environments.
evidence_of_usefulness: the six-category audit rejects every seeded contamination case
B3 is excluded because event year is outside the declared source-only contract
all learned baselines separate from no-skill under paired Brier uncertainty
B2 versus B5 remains unresolved, preventing a false winner declaration
the frozen predictions and manuscript values reconstruct exactly
substantive_result: Under the locked contract, every learned baseline improves over no-skill, the leading B2 and B5 models remain statistically unresolved, and the random-versus-sequence split diagnostic is small and reversed rather than evidence of optimistic random-split performance.
non_use_boundary: not cross-system or geographic generalization evidence
not proof that sequence grouping is unnecessary
not an untouched prospective evaluation because labels are public

independent_30_second_editor_test.reviewer: GPT-5.6 Sol, independent abstract-only three-reader test
independent_30_second_editor_test.quoted_summary: The benchmark helps engineers avoid invalid retrospective comparisons and unsupported winners, while requiring hidden data for confirmation and excluding operational use.
